To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
humoral immune responses to antigens of the trypomastigoite stages of Trypano-soma cruzi were detected by serological techniques in experimentally infected rodents.
humoral antibodies to metacycic trypomastigoes were first found on day 7 in rats and day 10 in mice.
the metacycic stage of the parasite is a potential antigenic source for the production of diagnostic reagents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an ELISA for detection of IgG and IgM antibodies to the metacycic stages of T. c. cruzi.
the development and evaluation of serological tests for the detection of antibodies against metacyclic forms of T. cruz.
the study of the immune response of rodents to T. cruzi.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the metacycic stage of T. cruzI has antigens in common with other stages of this parasite, and that these antigens are immunogenic and can be detected by serological tests during acute experimental infections.
the metacycic trypomastigiotes of T. cruzis are antigenically different from other forms of the parasite.
the humoral response in infected mice was more intense than that in infected rats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metacycic stage antigens of the Tulahuén T. cruzi strain are immunologically distinct from the other stages, and are useful in serodiagnostic procedures for the detection of T. cruz i antibodies.
the ELISA-Igm and the DAT are more sensitive than the ELISA-Igg and the IFAT, respectively, for detection of antibodies in infected animals during the early stages of infection.
the metacycic trypomastigiote antigen was a useful antigen for the serodiagnosis of acute Chagas' disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of metacyclic antigen for serodiagnosis is a promising tool.
the metacycic stage of T. cruz is a good target for serodiagnosis of acute Chagas disease.
metacyclogenesis is a dynamic process that involves the expression of a number of different proteins, and that the expression of these proteins varies with time.
